title: What exhaustion reaches, and what lies outside it — 5 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
What exhaustion reaches, and what lies outside it — 5 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the floor. 4 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide), 1 are proved for every value on the standard axioms. Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 1 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 6 pair(s); the theorems fall into 2 strand(s), the largest of 4. Most binding: bounds (4). 1 theorem(s) name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/reach.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 5 sealed receipts fold to 05528d94-5d7d-8142-9aa4-b7a650cd30e0. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (2, 6, 2, 3, 6, 4, 5). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: ledgerclaims.lean (3 observed, 0.44 expected, lift 6.76), coin.lean (4 observed, 0.67 expected, lift 6.01), elementary.lean (4 observed, 1.77 expected, lift 2.25). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.3; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.39. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 7.0% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. that no finite set contains every natural number is Euclid's argument in form and is as old as mathematics; the deposit claims none of it. What is its own here is the decision over its OWN bounds, and the statement of where that decision stops. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound — bounds.all (fun n => (List.range n).length == n && ¬ (List.range n).contains n) record
  2. the_successor_of_every_bound_lies_outside — bounds.all (fun n => ¬ (List.range n).contains (n + 1)) record
  3. doubling_the_domain_leaves_the_same_hole — bounds.all (fun n => ¬ (List.range (2 * n)).contains (2 * n)) record
  4. the_successor_leaves_every_domain_and_the_predecessor_returns — (bounds ++ [largestDomainHere]).all (fun n => n + 1 > n && (n + 1) - 1 == n && (n + 1) % 2 != n % 2) record
  5. the_predecessor_returns_every_successor — ∀ n : Nat, (n + 1) - 1 = n record
